newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANI sees Holter decision by Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: ANI sees Holter decision by Sept 30.

text.p: Australian National Industries Ltd said it expected to make an announcement about the future of German environmental engineering unit Holter by September 30.

"Negotiations are continuing at the moment and I don't want to put a firm date on it, but by September 30, we should be able to announce something," managing director Peter Stancliffe told Reuters in an interview.
He said negotiations between German government-owned Saarbergwerke AG and Holter about the possibility of a joint venture were proceeding well.
However, he said the companies now realised that some parts of both businesses should not be joined.

"It's become evident that there are parts of their environmental businesses that don't particularly appeal to us and parts of our environmental business that don't particularly appeal to them," Stancliffe said.

"We may have to adopt a composite solution where there will be parts of Holter that we will joint venture with Saarberg, parts of Holter that we may joint venture with others, parts of Holter that we dispose of altogether and there could be some that we will keep ourselves."
Stancliffe said ANI was currently involved in discussions with a number of mostly European companies regarding Holter.
He also said the company's original decision to invest in Holter was misguided.
"I think with the benefit of hindsight, it wasn't a particularly wise investment for ANI," he said.

"When you sit back and look at the strategic implications of it, they went into a business that they didn't know much about and it was 20,000 km away from home in an environment they didn't understand."
"Really, it was already a mature business when they bought in and about to go into decline. They couldn't have known that, but that's the way events have subsequently unfolded," Stancliffe said.
ANI earlier posted an annual net loss of A$213.19 million, compared to a profit of A$80.38 million in the previous year.
The result included an abnormal loss of A$198.55 million, which largely stemmed from a A$233.55 million writedown of the Holter assets.
ANI shares ended one cent down at A$1.01.
